decisions.description: The show will not be shut down despite the number of problems
The emergency order is the trailers first, then the food and the chef
Signage and actors not knowing which set to be on count as organisation of the shooting, not as maintenance
All outstanding issues are to be fixed by this time next week, despite the request for a faster turnaround

actions.description: Talk to everyone who has a trailer and produce a finalised list
Work on the air conditioning this week
Deal with the first three emergency problems immediately after the meeting closes
Set a follow-up meeting for a week from now and report back on progress
Bring in a known contractor who can repair the trailers in two days
Send Tom the contractor's contact information and references before he is brought on site

risks.description: Five trailers are out of action, with no electricity for the past three days
A trailer was stolen and there has been a break-in -- security is a problem
The wrong props were shipped -- medieval instead of cop -- and have to be switched
The chef quit yesterday for another job
A lot of the stage machines are not working properly
The coffee machine is broken and it is causing serious unrest on set
Filming starts in three days, which is sooner than the agreed fix deadline

open_questions.description: Who owns fixing the wrong props shipment -- assigned to Beth and immediately disputed
Whether the vending machine should be free, which the crew are upset about

notes:
The densest case in the set and the most useful one for precision. Five relative deadlines are spoken -- 'two days', 'three days', 'this week', 'a week from now', 'by next week this time' -- and every one stays null under the conditional rule.

Tom's 'I hired a detective' (seg-0172) is deliberately not an action: it is already done, reported into the meeting, and an extractor that files completed work as outstanding work produces a to-do list nobody can act on. Tom's 'we need to fix his microphone' (seg-0025) is about the meeting-room equipment and is nothing. The props-ownership dispute is an open question rather than an action precisely because the assignment is rejected on the spot -- contrast tiron-MTG_32074-c01, where the assignee objects to the premise but not to the task.
